title: Alexander Graham Bell's birth chart
metaDescription: Alexander Graham Bell's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.3° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mutable signs carry four of the nine placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. The mutable signs sit where one season is already becoming the next — the scheme’s translators.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 12.3° Pisces — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Moon. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Pisces and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Pisces (25.3°), Venus in Aries (0.8°), Mars in Capricorn (14.9°): a mind that absorbs before it argues, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Uranus — a square holding at 2.5°. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, the Sun sextile Mars at 2.5°, and Jupiter square Saturn at 3.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mercury in Pisces at 25.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Aries at 0.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Capricorn at 14.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Gemini at 8.2° is in detriment. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements water 3, fire 3, air 2, earth 1; modalities mutable 4, cardinal 4, fixed 1. Nothing here ran retrograde — all ten in direct motion that day.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.8° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
